question: Global Positioning System (GPS) is a network of several satellites orbiting the Earth at an approximate altitude of :
solution:
The correct answer is __**20,000 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The GPS satellites orbit the Earth at an approximate altitude of **20,000 km**.
 
• This altitude ensures that the satellites have a clear and unobstructed view of large portions of the Earth's surface, enabling accurate positioning.
 
• The altitude of 20,000 km is optimal for maintaining a stable orbit while providing a wide coverage area for GPS receivers on Earth.
 
• At this altitude, the satellites complete an orbit approximately every 12 hours, allowing for continuous and reliable global coverage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Positioning System (GPS):**

 
 
• GPS is a satellite-based navigation system that provides location and time information in all weather conditions, anywhere on or near the Earth.
 
• It was developed by the United States Department of Defense and originally intended for military applications but was made available for civilian use in the 1980s.
 
• The system consists of a constellation of at least 24 satellites orbiting the Earth, ground control stations, and GPS receivers used by individuals.
 
• GPS technology is widely used in various applications, including navigation for vehicles, aircraft, and ships, geolocation services, mapping, and timing synchronization.
 
 
 
• **Orbit Altitude:**
 
 
• The altitude at which a satellite orbits the Earth plays a crucial role in determining its coverage area and the frequency of its orbits.
 
• Satellites in higher orbits cover larger areas of the Earth but may have longer orbital periods, whereas satellites in lower orbits cover smaller areas but orbit more frequently.
 
• For GPS satellites, an altitude of 20,000 km is a compromise that allows for global coverage with a manageable number of satellites.
 
 
 
• **Orbital Period:**
 
 
• The orbital period is the time a satellite takes to complete one full orbit around the Earth.
 
• GPS satellites have an orbital period of approximately 12 hours, meaning they complete two full orbits in one day.
 
• This periodicity ensures that at least four satellites are visible from any point on the Earth's surface at any given time, which is necessary for accurate position determination.
